column1: # Honest-abstention realization frames — Reiter & Dale (2000) *Building Natural
# Language Generation Systems* (CUP), the realization stage: a communicative goal
# is realized by filling a stored linguistic template, NOT by concatenating an
# inline literal in code. These frames cover the FIFTH epistemic cell —
# vocabulary KNOWN, proposition OPEN — where both queried concepts resolve to
# loaded vocabulary but the relation between them is neither derivable nor
# disprovable from the loaded closure. Reiter (1978) closed-world assumption: the
# system names the boundary of its own knowledge, asserting neither a Yes, a No,
# (pragmatics::realize::realize_abstain) fills two typed slots it composes from
# the grammar in that module — never authored here:
#   {known}  the "both X and Y" nominal, each concept surface carrying its
#            determiner (select_determiner); e.g. "a cat and a dog".
#   {claim}  the relation sentence realized over the pair via sentence_relation
#            (the loaded connective, or the is-a copula default); e.g. "a cat is
#            a dog" — embedded UNDER "cannot confirm", so it asserts nothing.

column2: I know both {known}, but I cannot confirm from what I have loaded that {claim}.
